newsitem.title: MEXICO: Fewer Mexicans view United States favorably - poll.
newsitem.headline: Fewer Mexicans view United States favorably - poll.

text.p: Mexicans' view of the United States has soured considerably in the past year, although most still approve of their current visitor, U.S. President Bill Clinton, a poll showed on Tuesday.

Only 36 percent of Mexicans said they had a favorable view of their giant northern neighbor, compared to 62 percent that responded the same way during a poll a year ago, the survey by Reforma newspaper said.

Most Mexicans, however, still hold a favorable view of Clinton, who arrived here on Monday for his first state visit to Mexico and who in early 1995 engineered a $13.5 billion rescue package for the crisis-ridden Mexican economy.
Reforma said a recent dispute over Mexico's role in the drug trade had worsened Mexicans' view of the United States, a country that is usually respected here but seldom loved.

Mexico was angered earlier this year by the U.S. process of "certifying" those countries that helped the United States fight illegal drugs. The ones that did not make the grade faced economic sanctions.

Mexico was certified by the Clinton administration despite recent drug scandals, but Mexico, always rankled by what it perceives as U.S. bullying, said the process was an interference in its sovereign affairs.
Mexico's sovereignty has been a sensitive issue since the United States took away nearly half of its territory, including California, in 1848.
